problem:
Solve the inequality $-2{x}^{2}>10x+12$ and express the solution set in interval notation.

$x\in (${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$)$
worked_solution:
To solve this inequality using the graphical method, we first need to move all of the terms to the left-hand side so that the right-hand side is $0.$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}^{2} & >10x+12 \\ -2{x}^{2}-10x-12 & >0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find the values of $x$ for which the parabola $y=-2{x}^{2}-10x-12$ lies **above** the $x$-axis. Let's find the roots of the parabola by factoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}^{2}-10x-12 & =0 \\ 2{x}^{2}+10x+12 & =0 \\ (2{x}^{2}+6x)+(4x+12) & =0 \\ 2x(x+3)+4(x+3) & =0 \\ (2x+4)(x+3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We see that the roots are $x=-3$ and $x=-2,$ and we can graph the parabola as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14004892/assets/539e0e68f4a03c0bd4a309ebf2c4a00638d99c6eee233ca8f2cef3814e419c95.png)

Since we are interested in solving 

$$
-2{x}^{2}-10x-12>0,
$$

 
we look for the part of the parabola that is **above** the $x$-axis.

Based on the graph, the solution is $-3<x<-2.$

Using interval notation, we write $x\in (-3,-2).$
